nodes.action: migrated the schema without a backup
the corruption spread to the backups and took days to repair
took a full snapshot before the migration
the migration could always be rolled back
set up point-in-time recovery snapshots independent of the backup
deployed without running the test suite
set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests
switched to continuous replication since snapshots went stale by deploy time

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Morning, Dana. Got a minute? I need to talk through the schema migration I ran last night.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Sure, coffee's still hot. What happened? I saw the incident ticket this morning.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Yeah, so... I migrated the schema without taking a backup first. I know, I know. I thought it was a simple additive change, but it ended up corrupting a bunch of customer records.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Oh no. How bad? And wait, you said no backup? That's a pretty big miss.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: It's bad. The corruption spread to our nightly backups too, so we had to spend days repairing from partial logs. That was a nightmare.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: I can imagine. So what's the plan going forward? We can't have that happen again.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Agreed. I've already set up point-in-time recovery snapshots that are independent of the main backup system. That way, even if the backups get hit, we have a separate recovery path.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Good. And please tell me you're not going to deploy without running the test suite again either.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: That's the other thing. I deployed without running tests, and a regression slipped into production. I'm owning that.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Okay. So what are you doing about that?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I've set up a CI gate that blocks any merge unless tests pass. From now on, untested code never reaches production. That's a hard rule.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Alright. Let's review the incident details this afternoon, and I want to see those new snapshots in action.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Will do. Thanks for not yelling at me.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Hey Sam, quick check-in. How's the recovery going? And did the CI gate hold up?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Recovery is done, finally. And yes, the CI gate is working — we've had three merges blocked this week because someone forgot to run tests. It's annoying but it's working.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Good. And the point-in-time snapshots? Any issues?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: They're solid. I actually took a full snapshot before the migration this time, just to be extra safe. And the migration could always be rolled back if something went wrong.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: That's a big improvement from last week. So you're feeling confident?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Mostly. I mean, the snapshot gives us a clean restore point, and the rollback path is tested. I think we're in good shape.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Alright. Just remember, confidence is good, but verify everything before you touch production again.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Absolutely. I've learned my lesson.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Sam, I saw you pushed a new migration this morning. How did it go?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: It went... okay, but I have to be honest with you. I was wrong about the snapshot approach.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: What do you mean? You took a full snapshot before the migration, and you had rollback. That seemed solid.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Turns out that wasn't enough. The snapshot was taken at 2 AM, but by the time we deployed at 10 AM, there were six hours of new writes. When we had to roll back, we lost all that data.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Oh, that's a real problem. So what did you do?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: We replaced the snapshot-only approach with continuous replication. Now we're streaming changes to a separate cluster in real time, so the recovery point is seconds old, not hours.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: That makes sense. So snapshots are just a fallback now?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Exactly. Snapshots are still there for catastrophic failures, but continuous replication is the primary safety net. The old approach fell short because it didn't account for the gap between snapshot and deploy.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Good catch. And the CI gate is still holding?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Yes, untested code still never reaches production. That part is solid.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Alright. Let's document this new replication setup so the whole team knows. And thanks for being upfront about the snapshot limitation.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Thanks, Dana. I'd rather admit it now than hide it until the next incident.
